name: Global Payments Inc.
moat_justification: Real scale and switching costs in merchant acquiring, enlarged by Worldpay (6M+ merchant locations, ~$3.7T volume, 42% normalized adjusted operating margins), but acquiring is contested and price-pressured — Adyen/Stripe/Fiserv competition, SMB churn, no owned consumer network, growth bought via M&A, and 7.0x net-debt leverage limiting flexibility.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 4.2%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.8x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 7.0x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
one_liner: Solid-scale payments processor, moat 6/10 — does not clear 15% at $84.33 (13.7% weighted, IV $75.16); clears 15% at or below $75.16, and 7.0x net debt plus a deal-straddling TTM (Tier D on that pin) argue for demanding less.
moat_for: Combined scale — 6M+ merchant locations, ~$3.7T volume / ~94B transactions in 175+ countries
Switching friction for enterprise and integrated merchants via Genius POS / integrated software
Global distribution and bank/partner referral channels from legacy GPN and Worldpay
Proven margin structure — 42.0% normalized adjusted operating margin in Q2 2026, expanding
moat_against: Price-competitive acquiring; SMB churn and multi-homing; Stripe/Adyen win on developer experience and e-commerce
No owned consumer surface or network — rents card-network rails, exposed to interchange/regulatory pressure
Growth is bought, not organic — story depends on integrating Worldpay without attrition
Leverage (net debt 7.0x normalized OE) limits buyback and investment flexibility
